non_blocking_observations.observation: "stretch it across as many days as you need" is mild hyperbole. All-day edge-resize is the only interaction in the week adapter that does NOT participate in edge navigation: packages/web/src/views/Week/interaction/adapter/week-interaction.adapter.ts calls updateEdgeNavigation() only for the allDayDrag and timedDrag branches (lines ~375 and ~453), while the allDayResize branch just calls updateAllDayResizeInteractionVisual(). all-day.resize.ts also resolves the new edge via getNearestDayColumn(layout.dayColumns, ...), i.e. only columns currently rendered, and docs/frontend/week-drag-interaction.md states multi-day spans are clamped to the visible window. So one gesture can span at most the days visible in the current week window; longer spans need a second gesture after navigating. The underlying capability (cross-day stretching of an existing all-day event) is genuine, so this is a wording nit, not a false claim.
non_blocking_observations.suggested_wording: "...to stretch it across the days of the week" or "...across several days".

non_blocking_observations.observation: "When you edit or delete one, Compass asks what you actually meant" implies an up-front scope prompt. Per docs/acceptance/recurring-events.md line 28, the common path is act-then-promote: the change applies to This Event immediately, and a live toast then offers "1 This and Following" and "2 All". A genuine up-front choice exists only for structural recurrence-rule changes (Scenario 6), where "This Event" is not offered. The three scopes named in the prose are exactly right (RecurrenceScopeSchema in packages/core/src/types/event-command.contracts.ts is "this" | "thisAndFollowing" | "all"); only the timing of the prompt is glossed.
non_blocking_observations.suggested_wording: "...Compass applies it to that occurrence and offers to widen it — to this one and everything after it, or the entire series."

non_blocking_observations.observation: The bold lead-in "Multi-day select" names a selection gesture, but the blurb describes moving and stretching an existing event; nothing in the product selects a multi-day range. The body sentence ("an event doesn't have to stay where you first put it") disambiguates immediately and no create-by-drag claim is made, so FR-2.2 is satisfied — but the label is the one residual place a reader could infer drag-to-select-days. The label is mandated by FR-1.3, so changing it would need a requirements change, not a doc fix. "Multi-day events" would carry zero implication risk.

Stale evidence path in packet tp_docs_001: it cites packages/web/src/views/Calendar/components/Grid/allDay/useAllDayDraftCreation.ts, which does not exist on this branch. The real file is packages/web/src/grid/hooks/useAllDayDraftCreation.ts. The negative evidence itself is correct there (endDate = dayjs(startDate).add(1, "day"), a fixed single-day draft), so the FR-2.2 guardrail held; only the citation is wrong. Recorded for provenance hygiene; no artifact change required.

Both files_touched entries carry backup_path: null, while NFR-6 promises pre-write backups so /mmo:revert can restore pre-run state. Both files are tracked in git and the diff is trivially revertible via git checkout, so operational risk is nil, but the recorded provenance does not match the stated NFR. Outside this review's write scope.
